label: rem:hahn-exton-connection-prior-art
title: Prior art: a connection formula for the Hahn--Exton $q$-Bessel function
html:
Morita defines the Hahn--Exton q-Bessel function as

J^{(3)}_
u(x; q) =  rac{(q^{
u+1}; q)_\infty}{(q; q)_\infty}\, x^
u\, {}_1\varphi_1 ig(0; q^{
u+1}; q, q x^2 ig)

[morita2011, \S 1, p. 1]. Working with 0 < |q| < 1 and q = p^2, he uses the q-Borel and q-Laplace transformations of Zhang to write the solution of the Hahn--Exton equation at infinity as a heta_p-weighted combination of two {}_1\varphi_1 series in base p, valid for x otin [p^{ u+2}; p] [morita2011, Theorem 1, eq. (4), p. 3]. In the limit p o 1^- the formula becomes the classical expression of the Hankel function H^{(2)}_ u through J_ u and J_{- u} [morita2011, \S 1, p. 3].

The normalisation agrees with the one used in the second-order q-difference proof. The coefficient of (q x^2)^k in Morita's {}_1\varphi_1 is

 rac{(-1)^k\, q^{k(k-1)/2}}{(q; q)_k\, (q^{
u+1}; q)_k} = c_k,

so J^{(3)}_ u(x; q) = rac{(q^{ u+1}; q)_\infty}{(q; q)_\infty}\, x^ u\, g(q x^2), with g the corpus's generating function of the c_k. This is the precondition for citing the connection formula alongside the c_k recursion: both work with the same series.

What it does not supply: the connection formula is proved for 0 < |q| < 1, while the corpus evaluates at a substrate parameter greater than one, so using it there needs q replaced by q^{-1} and the formula rederived. And the p o 1^- limit recovers the classical Bessel connection; it says nothing about the c_k beyond the q-Bessel series itself.
